deploy-bot: [ALERT] Canary rollout: inference-svc v3.1 -> canary=20% | 15/50 canary pods CrashLoopBackOff / failing readiness probes. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/canary/inf-svc-v3.1 :rotating_light: Paging oncall.
Emma: I'm on it, seeing the pager. Kicking off quick checks.
Emma: kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=inference-svc -o wide -> a bunch of canary pods in CrashLoopBackOff, restartCount high. Logs show readiness probe returning 500 from sidecar envoy.
Aisha: Logs from model container show "Failed to open model config: no such file /mnt/models/config.json" — init container didn't mount model-config secret. weird.
Sanjay: We changed the scheduler code in v3.1 which also changed MODEL_PATH env to /models/v2. Init expects /app/models. Looks like the container now crashes trying to validate files on startup.
Liam: Also HPA noise: hpa/inference-svc-canary has targetCPUUtilizationPercentage=1 (typo) so it aggressively spun new pods, causing high pod churn and nodes filling up -> OOMs. I suspect combined causes amplified outages.
Emma: Confirmed HPA target is 1. That explains scaling churn on top of bad init. Customer impact: Grafana shows 4% of hosted requests 503s during window, top erroring accounts: acct-34, acct-78. Support already got a few DMs.
Emma: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) flip rollout feature flag off 2) set canary traffic to 0% 3) scale canary down 4) patch HPA to sane value 5) rollback deployment if needed. I'll take steps 1-3 now.
Emma: flip FF: rollout.inference_scheduler -> false (LaunchDarkly). @ops-bot please confirm toggle.
ops-bot: Feature flag rollout.inference_scheduler set to false by Emma at 2026-03-15T14:03Z :white_check_mark:
Emma: patch traffic router to weight canary=0 (curl https://router.internal/patch -d '{"service":"inference-svc","canary":0}') -> 200 OK.
Emma: kubectl scale deployment inference-svc-canary -n prod --replicas=0
Emma: kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=inference-svc | grep CrashLoopBackOff -> still shows old pods terminating, but no new canaries coming up.
Sanjay: I'm going to roll back the deployment to v3.0 if we still see instability after scale-down. Preparing rollback command: kubectl rollout undo deploy/inference-svc -n prod --to-revision=52
Aisha: HPA patch: kubectl patch hpa inference-svc -n prod --type='json' -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/targetCPUUtilizationPercentage","value":65}]' — applying now.
Liam: Noted a node drain earlier this morning (node-az2-017) that pushed extra pods onto dense nodes; not root cause but made OOM risk higher. We'll follow up with infra to check eviction/grace settings.
Emma: Customer comms: Support, please queue an incident banner for affected customers: "We detected elevated 503 errors for a subset of inference requests from 14:02-14:20 UTC. We've rolled back the canary and disabled the new scheduler. Engineers are investigating root cause."
Sanjay: After flag toggle & canary scale =0, error rate dropped to baseline within ~3 minutes. Rolling back to v3.0 now as a precaution.
deploy-bot: Rollout status: canary scaled to 0, flag disabled, HPA patched. Rollback initiated -> rollout/rollback started by Sanjay at 2026-03-15T14:08Z.
Emma: I'll keep monitoring for 30m and then hand off to Sanjay for postmortem. Oncall handoff ETA 14:40 UTC.
Liam: Leaving notes: collect kube events, pod logs (init & sidecar), hpa metrics, traffic router config, and LaunchDarkly toggle history.
Aisha: grabbing logs: kubectl logs <pod> -n prod -c init -> "mounts: secret not found: model-config" — will attach to the postmortem.
Emma: Thanks. If anything flares, ping me @emma. Otherwise I'll hand off at 14:40.
Sanjay: Acknowledged, will take PM for postmortem. I'll also open internal ticket to revert the env var change and add unit test for model path validation.
ops-bot: Incident note: mitigations applied at 2026-03-15T14:06Z (flag disabled, canary scaled to 0). Estimated customer impact: ~4% requests, ~18 minutes. Incident channel created: #inc-2693456789
Emma: handing off to Sanjay now for the writeup. Closing oncall for this active page. :white_check_mark:
Sanjay: Taking over postmortem actions and timeline capture.
